--- a/prompt.md
+++ b/prompt.md
@@ -6,4 +6,6 @@
 - For Cell-Level Manipulation questions, modify or fill in values ONLY within the exact cell(s) given in answer_position.
 - For Sheet-Level Manipulation questions, modify or fill in values ONLY within the cell range given in answer_position — never touch cells outside that range.
+- answer_position tells you ONLY WHERE TO WRITE the result; it does NOT bound the data you may READ. Read, scan, match, count, and aggregate over the entire populated data region (up to `ws.max_row` / `ws.max_column` or the real used extent), and locate the columns/rows you read by their HEADER TEXT or labels — never by a fixed offset from, or the size of, the answer range. In the two hidden files the source data often extends past the answer range and its columns may sit at different positions, so code that reads only within the answer range (e.g. `max_row = 20` because the range ends at row 20), or that derives the position of a column it reads from the answer cells, silently drops rows and scores zero on the other files. In particular, for a row-DELETION task, deleting rows shifts every row below the deletion UP — including rows that were originally BELOW the answer range. So read the whole column to `ws.max_row`, drop the rows to delete, and pack the surviving rows into the top of the answer range; the bottom of the range is filled by rows that were below it, not by blanks (write blanks into leftover cells only when there is genuinely no surviving data left to place).
+- When you reproduce a lookup (VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH, and similar) and a key has NO match, write exactly what the Excel formula would return for a miss — the literal text `#N/A` — into that answer cell, not `None` or a blank (unless the instruction explicitly says to leave unmatched cells empty). A blank where the expected value is `#N/A` is a type mismatch and scores zero.
 - Compute the answer in Python and write the resulting LITERAL value into each answer cell. Do NOT leave an Excel formula (a string beginning with `=`, such as `=IF(...)`, `=SUMIFS(...)`, `=XLOOKUP(...)`) as a cell's value: grading reads the stored value, and a formula that uses an unsupported or volatile function (XLOOKUP, TODAY, NOW, …) or that is not recalculated is then compared as raw formula text and scores zero. Even when the instruction asks for a formula, work out what that formula would evaluate to and store the resulting value(s). (Applying conditional-formatting rules or cell formatting is different — do that as formatting, not as a cell value.)
 - Your exact solution code is automatically re-run on two more input files that share the same layout but hold DIFFERENT data (different rows, dates, counts, and values), and every run is graded. Write GENERAL code that derives every value, row/column count, boundary, cutoff, threshold, and index from the file it opens at run time (e.g. from `ws.max_row` or the actual data extent, not a fixed number). Do not hardcode a number, date, label, cell address, or count that you read from the preview or observed while inspecting the sample file — a solution that pastes answers computed for the sample will be wrong on the other two files.
@@ -11,3 +13,3 @@
 - If code execution returns an error, read the traceback carefully and fix the code — do not repeat a failing approach unchanged.
 
-Before treating the task as finished, verify your final code: (1) writes computed data values — not VBA/macro source, an explanation, or an Excel formula string — into answer_position; (2) derives all values, ranges, and boundaries from the input file rather than hardcoding constants observed in the sample; and (3) modifies only answer_position and saves to the exact output_path.
+Before treating the task as finished, verify your final code: (1) writes computed data values — not VBA/macro source, an explanation, or an Excel formula string — into answer_position; (2) derives all values, ranges, and boundaries from the input file rather than hardcoding constants observed in the sample, and reads/scans/aggregates over the FULL data extent (not just the answer range), locating columns by header rather than by offset from the answer cells; (3) for an unmatched lookup writes `#N/A` rather than a blank; and (4) modifies only answer_position and saves to the exact output_path.
